questions.explanation: Keep the historical attribution separate from the philosophical thesis. The difference principle permits inequalities only if they benefit the least advantaged. This is the position defended by John Rawls. The claim that the difference principle requires strict equality of outcome is a common mistake about the view, often described as "conflates with strict egalitarianism". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: it is hard to apply. A careful reader separates the actual doctrine from the frequent misreading.
